text: Android + web: surface sync health (last-synced / pending / failing / blocked rows)

Done in f34ba3b (Android + web, per the chosen scope). 170 Android tests + lint
green; 40 web tests + oxlint + tsc --noEmit green.

Android: SyncStatus @Singleton (StateFlow<SyncState>: inProgress, lastSyncAt,
lastError, pendingCount, blockedCount), updated by SyncEngine on every run
(started/succeeded/failed/stoppedUnauthorized; recursive full-resync & 422-
quarantine retries re-report, so the UI settles on the innermost outcome; pending
recomputed post-merge). Surface = SyncStatusBar composable on Overview: quiet
recency line ("Synced 5 min ago · N pending") + loud tappable "N items need
attention" banner when blockedCount>0 that opens the list holding the first blocked
row (new ItemDao.firstBlockedItem / ItemsRepo.firstBlockedItem). SyncStatusBar is
reusable — T-36's list-screen recency indicator will read the same holder.

Web: no offline mirror (in-memory, cursor-0 on reload), so there is genuinely no
pending/blocked concept — only recency + failure, exactly as the ticket predicted.
useSync gained lastSyncAt (stamped in applyResponse, covering the normal and 410
paths); a SyncIndicator in the AppShell header renders "Syncing… / Synced X ago /
Sync failed" via pure syncStatusLabel (lib/syncStatus.ts) mirroring Android's
syncRecencyText.

Coordinated with T-36 as asked: one shared holder/surface, not two. T-36 adds
pull-to-refresh (manual syncNow + spinner) on ListScreen/Overview consuming this
same SyncStatus. Deliberately did NOT rebuild web_dist (committed bundle) — only
web source changed; a maintainer runs `npm run build` when they choose to ship it.

Note: the recency label reads current time at composition, so it refreshes on any
state change / sync rather than ticking every second — fine for a status line.
